fundamental.thesis: Ola Electric is India's largest EV two-wheeler OEM with vertically integrated battery ambitions (Ola Cell Technologies), but it remains deeply pre-profit and is facing a severe revenue downturn — Q1FY27 revenue fell 45% YoY to ₹455cr (from ₹828cr in Q1FY26), with PAT margin contracting sharply from -51.7% in Q1FY26 to -73.8% in Q1FY27, suggesting unit economics are deteriorating, not improving, as scale has shrunk. Using the appropriate yardstick for pre-profit/platform businesses (EV/Sales + growth-delivery + unit-economics trajectory), P/Sales of 8.29× for a company with deeply negative and declining revenues is expensive — there is zero growth delivery to justify a platform premium, and the EBITDA margin trend (-20.4% → -29.9%) is moving in the wrong direction. The single biggest risk is the auditor-qualified going concern assessment: management itself flagged negative operating cash flow of ₹215cr in Q1FY27, and a fresh rights issue announced September 28, 2026 confirms that the company requires continuous external capital — dilution and solvency risk are both live.

fundamental.thesis: Schaeffler India is a precision components manufacturer (bearings, transmission systems, clutch parts) for automotive and industrial customers, leveraging its German parent's technology IP and commanding ~79% of revenue from the Mobility segment with a quality premium over domestic-only ancillaries. H1 2026 showed revenue growth of +18.1% YoY to ₹5,346 cr and PAT growth of +19.1% to ₹642 cr, with EBITDA margin expanding from 19.6% to 20.1% across the tracked periods — an accelerating trajectory, though CFO/PAT of 0.61× is borderline weak and the ₹547 cr dividend paid against only ₹389 cr CFO raises a capital-allocation flag. Trailing P/E of 53.77× is nearly 2× the auto ancillary sector median of 18–28× and sits at P72 in the broad market; EV/EBITDA of 34.46× likewise approaches the upper end of even the capital-goods range (28–45×), making the stock expensive on both primary metrics — the forward P/E of 41.53× confirms growth is already priced in. The biggest risk is the premium valuation built on an uninterrupted growth story, which offers no margin of safety if growth decelerates due to auto-sector cyclicality, rising crude input costs, ongoing subsidiary losses (KRSV PAT −₹32 cr H1), or EV disruption of traditional drivetrain demand.

JSW Dulux (formerly Akzo Nobel India, bought by the JSW Group in Dec 2025) is a mid-sized decorative and industrial paints maker. It has been gaining volume, but its profit margins are under heavy pressure. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹1,927 cr, up 5.8% YoY as reported and up 20% on a like-for-like basis that excludes the divested Powder Coatings and IRC divisions, with volume up 23%. Reported revenue growth has improved from -4.0% (Q1FY26) to -2.8% (Q1FY27) to +5.8% (H1FY27). Over the same window PAT margin has fallen from 9.2% to 8.3% to 7.8%, and gross margin fell 1,180bp YoY to 35.4% as raw-material inflation outran price increases. Implied Q2 PAT of about ₹71 cr is below Q1's ₹80 cr. I used forward P/E rather than trailing P/E. The 7.45× trailing P/E and the P4 'cheap vs peers' rank are not real: they are inflated by the ₹1,874 cr one-off gain from the divestiture in H1 FY26, and the reported -91.5% H1 PAT drop is distorted by that same gain. On forward P/E of 31.3× (P67 vs the broad market) and P/B of 6.0×, the stock is fair: below listed paint leaders but not cheap for a business whose margins are falling. Sell-side FY-EPS estimates have been cut 8.8% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that crude is near $91 and rising, which pushes up paint raw-material costs and could cut margins further while the new JSW owners push for market share.

BLS International runs outsourced visa and consular processing for foreign governments, where it earns high margins (H1FY27 segment margin 39.7%). It also has a fast-growing but low-margin Digital Services and e-governance arm (H1FY27 revenue ₹793 cr, up 50% YoY, at only a 6.2% margin). Revenue growth picked up from +25.3% YoY in Q1FY27 to +32.0% in Q2FY27 (₹973 cr), but profit is not keeping pace. Q2 PAT rose only 8.6% to ₹202 cr, PAT margin fell from 25.2% to 20.8% YoY, and EBITDA margin dropped from about 30% in FY26 to 25.5%. The causes are the shift toward the low-margin digital business and costs from the Atyati and Trefeddian Hotel acquisitions. On valuation we used EV/EBITDA and P/E rather than the sector card's 60-100x consumer-discretionary multiples, because this is a services contractor, not a premium consumer franchise. At 10.2x EV/EBITDA and 13.8x trailing P/E (11.0x forward), the stock sits around the cheapest 11% of the broad market and well below the market median of 35x P/E, and net cash of ₹1,665 cr (about 17% of market cap) supports that. So we grade it cheap, though the stock near its 52-week low shows the market is already pricing in the falling margins. The main risk is that margins keep sliding as the digital business grows and acquired businesses are integrated, which would leave earnings flat even while revenue grows.

The main risk is that the high multiple is priced for growth while margins and cash conversion keep slipping.

Trailing P/E of 46x is above the 22–30x IT range and about 31% above the broad-market median (P66). Forward P/E is at the top of that range, and the stock sits at 25.5% of its 52-week range. Margins are shrinking because employee costs rose 21.8% YoY and now take 68.8% of revenue, and outside Industrials (+21.4%) the segments are barely growing (Financial Services +3.5%, CPG/Retail +2.7%). On valuation I used the IT sector P/E range plus EV/EBITDA. Trailing P/E is 32.3x, a little above the 22–30x IT range. Forward P/E is 22.1x and EV/EBITDA is 24.2x, close to the broad-market median (about P50). That makes it fair overall, not cheap, since estimates are being cut. The biggest worry is earnings quality: in H1 only about 26% of profit turned into operating cash (CFO/PAT 0.26x, down from 0.60x), and analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 6% over 90 days. Both suggest the growth premium could shrink further.

The biggest risk is that growth keeps slowing while the offline build-out and the Utkarsh Classes acquisition squeeze margins, which would knock the rich multiple down sharply.

fundamental.thesis: Tata Power is India's largest integrated power utility — spanning thermal generation (Mundra), renewables (4+ GW operational, TP Solar manufacturing), and T&D distribution in Mumbai/Delhi — and is structurally positioned at the intersection of India's energy-transition and electrification themes. Q1FY27 revenue grew 5.6% YoY to ₹19,051 cr with PAT up 11.0% YoY to ₹1,401 cr (7.4% PAT margin), representing a meaningful acceleration from the -1.8% revenue trough of 9MFY26 — EBITDA margin expanded to 23.6% from 21.2% YoY driven by a high-margin renewables segment (32.1% EBITDA margin) and T&D revenue surging 13.5% YoY; TP Solar's 2GW H1FY27 output milestone further validates the manufacturing flywheel. Using EV/EBITDA of 15.23× as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive hybrid (the sector card explicitly calls for EV/EBITDA over P/E), Tata Power sits at the 26th percentile vs broad-market peers and 34.7% below the median — fairly valued to modestly cheap — though the trailing P/E of 34.41× far exceeds the 10–18× utilities sector benchmark, an artefact of high financial leverage (D/E 168×) and a renewable-growth premium embedded in the equity. The single biggest risk is a USD 490 million (≈₹4,100 cr) contingent SIAC arbitration liability (Kleros Capital NDA breach) with no provision recorded — an adverse ruling would effectively erase roughly three full quarters of PAT and could necessitate dilutive equity issuance against an already stretched balance sheet.

Nava is a diversified midcap that earns money from a coal-fired power plant and coal mining in Zambia (MEL), merchant and captive thermal power in India, and ferro-alloy (silico-manganese) production in Odisha. It is a power-and-metals cyclical, not a regulated utility like NTPC or POWERGRID. In Q1FY27, consolidated revenue was ₹1,212 cr, up only 1.6% YoY. PAT was ₹333 cr, down 16.6% YoY from ₹399 cr, and EBITDA fell 7.0% YoY to ₹584 cr. Revenue growth has slowed from +20.9% in Q3FY26 to +7.7% for FY26 and +1.6% now. The big QoQ jump (PAT +144%) mostly recovers from a weak Q4, helped by higher plant load factors (India 85.4%, Zambia 89.3%), and does not mark a new uptrend. Cash conversion is a real positive: operating cash flow was 2.9x PAT in FY26, with ₹505 cr of free cash flow. I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA because this is a capital-intensive business. At 10.0x EV/EBITDA, 1.79x P/B and 20.9x trailing P/E, the stock sits in the bottom quartile of the broad market (P10 on EV/EBITDA, P14 on P/B), but its P/E is above the 10–18x utilities band. Once you allow for Zambia country risk and cyclical earnings, I'd call it fair rather than clearly cheap. The near-term risks are the Q2FY27 results on 12 Nov 2026, the Odisha 60MW plant shutdown in September, and the 300MW MEL Phase 2 delay to mid-2028, which pushes out the next growth step.

fundamental.thesis: Vodafone Idea is the third and weakest player in India's telecom market, which has roughly 2.5 players. It runs on a large government-linked debt and dues structure and is trying a capex-led turnaround while Jio and Airtel hold most of the industry's revenue. In Q1FY27, revenue grew 6.0% YoY to ₹11,689 cr, up from +1.9% in Q3FY26, and EBITDA margin rose to 43.1% from 42.5%; ARPU climbed 10.2% YoY to ₹195 and subscribers grew for the first time since the merger (193.1 mn), but the PAT loss was still ₹3,754 cr, a -32.1% margin, after ₹5,120 cr of finance costs and ₹5,467 cr of D&A. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for capital-intensive telecom. On that basis the stock is expensive: 28.6x versus the card's 9–12x norm for Indian mobile operators, 63rd percentile against the broad market, and the price sits at 90% of its 52-week range. The 4.3x trailing P/E is meaningless because a one-off FY26 gain distorts it, book value is negative, and the forward P/E is also negative. The biggest risk is solvency: negative net worth of ₹38,327 cr, deferred spectrum and AGR dues of about ₹1.56L cr with ₹9,259 cr due by June 2027, and a turnaround that depends on lender support and ₹45,000 cr of capex. The Q2FY27 results on 12 Nov are a near-term event risk.

fundamental.thesis: Indus Towers rents mobile tower space to telecom operators, with about 2.7 lakh towers and 1.63 tenants per tower in the latest KPI data. Revenue growth slowed from +7.9% in Q3 FY26 to +4.6% in Q1 FY27 and +4.0% (₹8,516 cr) in Q2 FY27, while PAT growth went from +0.5% to -2.5% (₹1,793 cr), leaving H1 PAT down 1.6% at ₹3,519 cr; I treated the row labelled Q2FY26 as Q2 FY27 because H1 less Q1 revenue is exactly ₹8,516 cr, but the same subtraction gives PAT of ₹1,773 cr and the 55.3% H1 EBITDA margin sits above both quarters (53.6% and 54.4%), so the margin figures are only approximate. On EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for capital-intensive businesses, 8.12× is below its 9-12× range, which is written for mobile operators rather than tower companies, so I grade the stock cheap, helped by a 15.29× trailing P/E and H1 free cash flow of ₹4,332 cr, though the bottom-quartile peer ranks are against the broad market rather than true peers and slowing growth justifies part of the discount. The biggest risk is a major customer under AGR-related stress that is paying only monthly billings, which has already kept ₹198 cr of revenue unrecognised in H1, while the 13.31× forward P/E assumes roughly 15% EPS growth even as PAT falls and estimates are being cut (FY EPS -1.4% over 90 days); leverage is also unclear, because the reported 2.33× net debt/EBITDA does not reconcile with debt of about ₹21,000 cr implied by the 53% debt/equity, or roughly 1.1× annualised EBITDA.

fundamental.thesis: ITI Limited is a Government of India-owned telecom equipment manufacturer (PSU under Department of Telecommunications) engaged in defence communication, broadband gear, and telecom network products — a structurally impaired business currently in a BIFR-supervised revival plan, NOT a telecom service operator and therefore the Telecom sector card (ARPU/EBITDA framework) does not apply here. Revenue declined -14.6% YoY in Q1 FY27 (₹425 cr vs ₹498 cr), continuing a severe multi-quarter deceleration that saw -39.5% over 9MFY26 and -32.2% over H1FY26; PAT remains deeply negative at -₹32 cr (-7.4% margin), though marginally better than -₹64 cr a year ago — the 'PAT margin expanding' trajectory signal is misleading as it simply reflects a slightly smaller loss on a shrinking revenue base. Valuation is strikingly expensive: trailing P/E of 79.4× sits at P87 among 473 broad-market peers (+126% premium to market median of 35.2×) and EV/EBITDA of 483× is economically meaningless for a loss-making entity — the ₹25,371 cr market cap is pricing in the ₹8,280 cr ASCON Phase IV defence order optionality and GoI backing, not current earnings power. The single biggest risk is the material audit qualification — auditors issued a disclaimer of opinion citing Ind AS 115 revenue recognition failures on complex engineering contracts, inventory obsolescence, and inadequate internal controls, which means reported numbers cannot be relied upon and could be restated downward.

fundamental.thesis: Phoenix Mills is India's dominant organised retail mall operator (not primarily a residential developer) — its Property & Related Services segment runs ~57% EBITDA margins on a portfolio of high-footfall malls, making it closer to a retail REIT-annuity than a cycle-linked developer. In Q1FY27, consolidated revenue grew +12.8% YoY to ₹1,075 cr — a clear acceleration from +5.4% in Q1FY26 — with PAT rising faster at +22.9% to ₹395 cr and PAT margin expanding to 36.7% from 25.3%; the EBITDA margin, however, contracted to 54.7% from 62.5% quarter-on-quarter, the residential segment effectively shut down at -92% YoY, and FY26 full-year CFO/PAT of 0.34× signals that a large portion of reported earnings is not yet converting to operating cash. Per the sector card, P/E is structurally meaningless for real estate; using EV/EBITDA (the correct yardstick for this capital-intensive model), PHOENIXLTD trades at 28.3× against a broad-market median of 23.3× (P62 rank, +21% premium) — fairly valued given the annuity-quality mall revenues, but not cheap, and the premium leaves no margin of safety against balance-sheet stress. The thesis is undermined by D/E of 37.21×, ₹2,898 cr of goodwill impairments booked in FY26, one subsidiary not on a going-concern basis, 90-day EPS estimate cuts of ~5%, and a RISK_OFF macro regime with Real Estate formally underweighted in sector tilts.

Mahanagar Gas is the dominant city gas distributor in Mumbai, Thane and Raigad, supplying CNG to vehicles and piped gas to homes and businesses, so its earnings depend on the gap between what it pays for gas and what it can charge customers. Sales are growing but profit is shrinking. H1FY27 revenue rose 18.5% YoY to Rs 5,377 cr, while PAT fell 35.7% to Rs 328 cr. By our calculation, Q2FY27 revenue was about Rs 2,778 cr (+23% YoY) and PAT about Rs 135 cr (about -29% YoY), the third straight period of shrinking margins: EBITDA margin fell from 20.6% in 9MFY26 to 14.3% in Q1 and 12.7% in H1. Because this is a capital-intensive, regulated-style utility, we graded valuation on EV/EBITDA (7.4x) and P/E (14.2x trailing, 12.9x forward), both inside the 10-18x Utilities / Energy range, so we call it fair. The low multiple reflects the margin squeeze and should not be read as a bargain; the broad-market peer rank is a fallback with no true gas-distribution peers and carries little weight. The biggest risk is that gas costs keep rising faster than prices, given cuts to cheaper domestic gas allocation, more costly gas in the mix and crude near $91.

fundamental.thesis: Brigade Enterprises is a Bengaluru-focused developer with residential projects plus a steady leasing and hospitality annuity business; its leasing segment earns a 67.5% margin and grew 1.3% YoY. H1FY27 consolidated revenue fell 13.2% YoY to ₹2,312 cr, mainly because real-estate segment revenue dropped 26.6% to ₹1,374 cr. PAT still rose 32.7% to ₹436 cr, lifting the PAT margin to 18.9%, and the implied Q2 alone (about ₹1,133 cr revenue, ₹219 cr PAT) was similar to Q1. The forward-looking metrics are thin: Q1FY27 bookings were ₹1,061 cr on 0.74 mn sq ft and collections were ₹1,856 cr, with no year-ago figure to show the trend. Cash conversion weakened to 0.42x CFO/PAT in H1, against 1.63x in Q1. Following the sector card, I judged valuation on bookings, collections and net debt, not P/E. On that basis, net debt/EBITDA of 2.1x, gross D/E of 0.79x, a forward P/E of 17x and a price at 53% of its 52-week range point to fair, not cheap, value. The snapshot's P/B of 30.5x and EV/EBITDA of 143.6x look like data errors, since net worth of about ₹7,155 cr against a ₹20,830 cr market cap implies P/B near 2.9x. The biggest risks are the revoked environmental clearance on a large Chennai project and a ₹860 cr landowner JDA dispute. Analysts also cut current-year EPS estimates by 6.1% in the last 30 days.

fundamental.thesis: NHPC is India's largest hydropower generator, a government-owned company that earns a regulated return on the power plants it has commissioned, so its profits grow with commissioned capacity rather than with power prices; the Subansiri Lower project (1,250 MW of a planned 2,000 MW now running) is its main growth driver. In H1 FY27, revenue grew 26.0% YoY to ₹8,291 cr and PAT grew 20.6% to ₹2,836 cr (PAT margin 34.2%), faster than the +14.5% revenue growth a year earlier; however, ₹918 cr of that revenue is provisional Parbati-II income still awaiting CERC tariff approval, finance costs more than doubled (+115%), and EBITDA margin fell from 65.7% to 63.0%. Using EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital-intensive utilities, NHPC trades at 25.5x, slightly above the broad-market median of 23.3x; its trailing P/E of 27.4x is well above the 10–18x utilities range, and a P/B of 1.85x against an ROE of only 9% is not cheap, so I grade it expensive on current earnings. The low forward P/E of 11.9x (estimates raised 3.9% over 90 days) and the stock sitting near the bottom of its 52-week range are the main counterpoints. The biggest risk is that heavy borrowing (net debt about ₹56,700 cr, debt/equity 1.36, negative free cash flow) keeps pushing up interest costs faster than new capacity adds earnings, especially if the remaining Subansiri units are delayed or the Parbati-II provisional revenue is cut when CERC sets the tariff.

fundamental.thesis: ICICI Bank is India's second-largest private-sector bank, with a large retail and business-banking franchise and subsidiaries in life and general insurance. In Q2FY27, consolidated revenue rose 15.8% YoY to ₹88,161cr, up from +6.9% growth in Q1. PAT rose 21.5% YoY to ₹17,389cr, up from +12.6%, but PAT margin slipped from 20.4% to 19.7%. Net interest margin (NIM) has also fallen from 4.36% to 4.18% in one quarter, and the share of low-cost CASA deposits dropped from 38.1% to 35.8%; on the positive side, gross NPA improved to 1.2% and net NPA to 0.30%, with provision coverage at 75%. Following the sector card, I value lenders on price-to-book against ROE: P/B of 2.48x with a 16.4% ROE is fair for a top-quality bank, even though it ranks P93 (expensive) on P/B among its 15 bank peers, and the stock sits at 22% of its 52-week range, which makes for a reasonable entry point. The biggest risk is that management expects two more 25bp repo hikes and says NIM will only bottom after Q3, so margins could compress further before they recover.

Grasim is an Aditya Birla holding company with cement (through UltraTech), cellulose fibre (VSF), chemicals, the Birla Opus paints entry, renewables and financial services (Aditya Birla Capital) all reported in one set of accounts, so I judged it as a conglomerate rather than a pure materials stock. Consolidated revenue in Q1 FY27 was ₹48,716 cr, up 21.4% YoY, and PAT was ₹3,846 cr, up 38.8%, continuing five quarters of 17-25% revenue growth. The PAT margin jumped from about 1.4-3% to 7.9%, but the trend table has a mislabelled 'FY26' row and mixes consolidated and attributable profit, so I'm treating that margin jump as unconfirmed rather than a clean improvement. In cement, the main earnings driver, volume rose 15% and profit per tonne (EBITDA) held at a healthy ₹1,051-1,253 through FY26. Because this is a capital-heavy group, I used EV/EBITDA to grade valuation: at 13.2x it is 26% below the sector median (P27), and P/B of 2.1x is cheap against peers (P19). That cheapness is largely explained by a weak 6.3% ROE, the lending book inside the group and the usual holding-company discount. Trailing P/E of 42x (P73) is above the 12-22x materials range, but forward P/E of 21x is in line with peers, so overall valuation is fair. fundamental.thesis: InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo) is India's largest airline, with a 442-aircraft fleet, and its results are driven mainly by fares, fuel costs and the rupee rather than the order-book measures in the Industrials sector card. On the yardstick the sector card names for oil marketing companies (P/E plus dividend yield, EV/EBITDA as a cross-check), the stock looks low on trailing numbers: P/E 4.4x against a peer median of 9.2x, EV/EBITDA 4.1x against 6.1x, and P/B 0.85x with 21% ROE. Those trailing numbers are inflated by an unusually strong Q2, though. Forward P/E is 7.7x, close to the 8.1x peer median and higher than trailing, which means analysts expect earnings to fall, so I grade it fair: priced for policy risk rather than mispriced. The biggest risk is crude at about $91 and rising while retail fuel prices stay frozen, which could push marketing margins back toward Q1-style losses; earnings are also turning into cash poorly (H1 CFO/PAT 0.48x, free cash flow ₹-1,450 cr).

fundamental.thesis: Bajaj Auto makes two- and three-wheelers and is a leading Indian exporter, with about 48% of India's two-wheeler exports and 63% of its three-wheeler exports in H1, plus a 23% Q2 market share for its Chetak electric scooter. Q2FY27 consolidated revenue rose 60% YoY to Rs 25,126 cr and PAT rose 60% to Rs 3,400 cr, but the 'accelerating' revenue signal (+19% to +32% to +60%) looks inflated by full consolidation of KTM, so unit volumes are the better guide, and their growth slowed from +29% in Q1 to +20% in Q2 while PAT margin fell from 17.1% in Q4FY26 to 14.9% and then 13.5%. Valuation is fair on the auto card's P/E yardstick, cross-checked with EV/EBITDA because the Rs 25,126 cr revenue includes low-margin consolidation effects: trailing P/E of 26.6x is inside the 18-30x OEM range and 1.9% below the 27.1x peer median (P40), while EV/EBITDA of 19.8x is 8.1% above the peer median (P67) and the stock sits at 85% of its 52-week range, which limits upside despite FY EPS estimates rising 10.3% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that input-cost inflation of about 8% of revenue in H1, only about 60% recovered through pricing, continues into Q3 just as rupee support fades and rural demand weakens; some data also conflicts, including a stale-filing flag, a yfinance revenue mismatch and an implausible 145% dividend yield, so those items were not relied on.

Coal India is the state-controlled near-monopoly coal miner that supplies most of India's thermal power fuel, and it earns a steady return from domestic volumes, e-auction premiums and a high dividend payout. In H1 FY27 revenue rose +13.8% YoY to ₹90,434 cr and PAT rose +18.9% to ₹15,397 cr (PAT margin 17.0%), recovering from a weak FY26 (revenue -0.5%, PAT -12.3%). The quality of that growth is mixed: offtake rose +7.6% to 384.2 MT while production fell -2% to 321 MT, so part of the growth came from selling down inventory, which fell 49% to 130.3 MT. Cash conversion was strong (CFO/PAT 2.21x, FCF ₹26,270 cr). I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA plus P/E and yield, as the sector card prescribes for PSU energy names. At 6.1x EV/EBITDA and 9.2x trailing P/E the stock sits exactly at the Energy peer median (P50) and inside the 6–10x policy-priced band, so it is fair, not cheap. The stock is at 85% of its 52-week range and EPS estimates are drifting slightly lower (-0.9% over 30d), which limits upside. The main risk is that volume growth cannot continue once the inventory buffer is used up while production is still falling, and administered pricing caps any offset from price.

fundamental.thesis: IndusInd Bank is a mid-sized private lender, heavy on vehicle finance (28% of loans, 58% retail), that is still rebuilding after the FY26 accounting-discrepancy year in which full-year PAT fell 65% to ₹891 cr and ROA dropped to 0.17%. Per the H1FY27 filing, total income rose 26.8% YoY to ₹23,873 cr and PAT rose 36.4% to ₹2,279 cr, but this flatters the core business: the comparison base includes a Q2FY26 loss, Q1FY27 includes a one-off ₹868 cr IFR transfer, and operating profit actually fell 7.9% YoY to ₹10,323 cr. Loan growth has recovered from -8.5% (FY26) to +11% YoY, but NIM has slipped to 3.23% from 3.39–3.48%, credit cost is elevated at 1.4%, cost-to-income is high at 57.9%, and annualised Q2 ROE is only 7.4%. Using the bank yardstick (P/B with ROE, ignoring the distorted 80× trailing P/E), a P/B of 1.08× (P29 vs peers, 26% below the 1.5× median) fits sub-par returns of about 7% ROE, so the valuation is fair rather than cheap; the cheap case only holds if ROE recovers toward 12%+. The biggest risk is that the earnings recovery stalls as NIM compression and above-normal vehicle and microfinance credit costs hold ROA under 1%.

fundamental.thesis: Apollo Hospitals is India's largest private healthcare network, integrating hospital services (~70% occupancy in Q1FY27, up from 65% a year ago), 7,100+ pharmacy stores, diagnostics, and the Apollo 24/7 digital platform — a diversified moat no single peer can replicate at scale. Q1FY27 revenue was ₹7,043 cr (+21% YoY, accelerating from +13% in Q2FY26) with PAT of ₹581 cr (+34% YoY) and PAT margin expanding to 8.2% from 7.4% in Q1FY26 — both revenue growth and margins have moved consistently upward across six consecutive quarters. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive hospital business (per sector card guidance), Apollo trades at 33.5× vs a healthcare peer median of 23.3×, a 44% premium placing it at P75 in the sector — graded expensive, though the forward P/E of 39.1× (vs trailing 61.75×) signals meaningful earnings growth already anticipated by the market; the stock sits at 87.4% of its 52-week range, leaving limited margin of safety. The biggest risk is high leverage (D/E 85.15) coinciding with a 5,800-bed capex cycle; a stall in occupancy expansion or rising financing costs would rapidly de-rate the premium multiple in the current RISK_OFF, rising-rate tape.

fundamental.thesis: BPCL is a large state-run refiner and fuel retailer whose earnings depend heavily on crude prices and government pricing policy. H1 FY27 revenue rose 26.3% YoY to ₹317,345 cr, but this looks mostly price-led (H1 throughput +1.6%, domestic sales +3.2%), while PAT fell 77.0% to ₹2,990 cr and margins contracted from FY26 levels (EBITDA 8.0% to 2.9%, PAT 4.9% to 0.9%); Q2 PAT recovered from a ₹3,962 cr Q1 loss to ₹4,993 cr but was still down 22.5% YoY, even with GRM at $32.53/bbl (Q1: $41.41), and Q2 revenue is missing from the filing data while Q1 and Q2 PAT sum to only ₹1,031 cr against the reported H1 figure, so these numbers need checking. Using the sector card's P/E-plus-yield yardstick for oil marketers, valuation is fair rather than cheap: the 4.71x trailing P/E and 3.74x EV/EBITDA are below the peer medians of 9.2x and 6.1x, but the P/E appears to reflect older, peak earnings, since our rough trailing-12-month PAT of ₹15,800 cr implies about 7.6x, in line with the 7.19x forward P/E and inside the 6-10x policy-priced range, and the 678% dividend yield is a clear data error so yield could not be assessed. fundamental.thesis: SBI Life is a large listed Indian life insurer with a market cap of about ₹1.8L cr, and the sector card says to judge it on new business value (VNB), APE growth and price-to-embedded-value (P/EV), not PAT. H1 FY27 shows embedded value of ₹87,350 cr and six-month VNB of ₹3,270 cr, but no reliable growth rate can be calculated because the year-ago figures (₹7,600 cr and ₹275 cr) look like unit errors; the last usable revenue and PAT growth is Q1 FY27 at +16.9% and +21.9%, revenue growth has stayed in a +16% to +19% range rather than clearly slowing as the trend signal says, and the table mixes quarterly and cumulative periods. On P/EV, the stock trades at about 2.1x (₹1.8L cr / ₹87,350 cr), which I grade fair on a provisional basis because no peer or historical P/EV is provided; the 71.7x trailing P/E (peer median 53.7x) is not the right yardstick, and the 15% of 52-week range position offers a better entry only if growth holds, while the 15.0% dividend yield looks like a data error and is ignored. The main concern is business quality: 13-month persistency has slipped from 87.11% in H1 FY26 to 84.35% in Q1 FY27 and the expense ratio has risen from 10.9% to 12.05%, while FY EPS estimates have edged down about 1% over 90 days despite 34 of 35 analysts rating it a buy.

Pidilite Industries is India's leading adhesives and sealants company (Fevicol, Dr. Fixit), a consumer franchise with strong pricing power, not a commodity chemicals business. The latest quarter extracted is Q1FY27, where revenue was ₹4,552 cr (+21.3% YoY) and PAT was ₹884 cr (+29.8% YoY), with EBITDA margin up to 28.6% from 23.4% in Q4FY26 and PAT margin up to 19.4% from 16.8% in FY26. Revenue growth has picked up from +11.1% for FY26 and +15.3% in Q4FY26. However, the Q2FY27 numbers filed on 2026-10-28 were not extracted, and the Q3FY26 revenue of ₹996 cr looks like a partial or bad row, so the trend is incomplete. I graded valuation on the sector card's consumer-franchise yardstick of 30–60× P/E for paints and adhesives, not the cyclical Materials median. On that basis it is fair but near the top of the band: trailing P/E is 57.1× and forward P/E is 46.8×, which assumes earnings keep growing. The stock sits at P93–P100 among Materials peers, but most of those peers are steel and metals cyclicals, so that ranking overstates how expensive it is. The stock is mid-range in its 52-week band (49.9%), and the average analyst target is only +6.8% above the price. The biggest risk is that a premium multiple leaves no room for a growth slowdown, and the slight 30-day EPS estimate cuts (-1.7%) are an early warning to watch. The snapshot's 77% dividend yield and 3.78 debt/equity look like data errors for a business that is close to debt-free, so I ignored them.

fundamental.thesis: Cholamandalam Investment is a large, diversified non-bank lender focused on vehicle, MSME/property-backed and consumer loans, with AUM growth accelerating from +21% in Q4 FY26 to +23% in Q1 and +24.7% in H1 FY27. H1 FY27 revenue rose 22.6% YoY to about Rs 18,351 cr and PAT rose 43.3% to Rs 3,284 cr, but Q2 figures derived by subtracting Q1 from H1 show revenue growth of about +23% and PAT growth slowing from +45.5% to about +41%, with PAT slipping sequentially from Rs 1,654 cr to about Rs 1,630 cr and PAT margin falling from about 18.5% to about 17.3%; NIM was flat at 8.0% against Q4 FY26, while credit cost eased from 1.5% to 1.4%. On the P/B-versus-ROE yardstick for lenders, the stock looks expensive at 4.62x book with ROE of 19-20%, which is at P89 of peers and 51.5% above the 3.0x median, although strong growth and low-priced state-owned peers such as PFC and RECLTD explain part of the premium; the 26.77x trailing P/E (P78) appears to use FY26 EPS, and is closer to 23x on my estimate of trailing-twelve-month PAT. The biggest risk is that this premium leaves little room for credit slippage, as gross NPA of 4.44% is better than 4.57% a year ago but above 4.36% in March 2026, Ind AS provision cover has fallen from 47.29% to 45.32% since March, and consumer-loan losses are elevated at 2.2%.

LIC is India's dominant life insurer, with a 58.8% share of first-year premium income (37.5% in individual policies, 70.5% in group) and ₹59.6L cr of assets under management. In H1FY27, gross premium income grew 11.6% YoY to ₹2,75,423 cr, up from +4.8% growth in H1FY26. PAT rose 22.0% to ₹25,699 cr, though PAT margin slipped from 9.8% to 9.3%. The better quality signal is that Value of New Business (VNB, the profit expected from new policies) grew 34% to ₹6,846 cr, and VNB margin widened 470 bps to 22.3%. Weaker spots: policy count fell 2.25%, individual non-participating APE fell 6%, and Indian Embedded Value (EV) slipped 1.95% to ₹7,97,378 cr. For valuation I used P/EV, the right yardstick for life insurers, and ignored P/E. A market cap of about ₹5.0L cr against EV of ₹7.97L cr gives P/EV of roughly 0.63×, well below book embedded value. LIC is also the cheapest of its 4 listed life-insurance peers on every multiple (P/B 2.05× vs a 6.8× peer median), so I grade it cheap, even after allowing a discount for state ownership and a lower-margin product mix. The main risk to this view is that EV and individual-policy volumes are both falling while VNB margin rises, which may mean growth relies on a mix shift and could be squeezed by IRDAI's proposed commission rule changes.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Power is India's largest private thermal generator (18.3 GW operating, 23.7 GW under construction), with about 88-95% of capacity tied to long-term PPAs and the rest sold on the merchant market, which makes it a power-cycle business rather than a regulated annuity like NTPC or POWERGRID. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.5% YoY to Rs 17,528 cr, recovering from -3.5% in FY26 to +10.0% in Q4 FY26 and +33.9% in Q1 FY27, though growth eased slightly in Q2; reported PAT of Rs 7,019 cr (+141.5%, 40.0% margin) includes a one-time Rs 2,422 cr recovery of past dues, so underlying PAT is closer to Rs 4,600 cr (about 26% margin), and EBITDA margin fell from 44.3% to 36.1% as fuel costs jumped 41.8%. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive generator: at 25.2x it is 118% above the Utilities peer median of 11.6x, and trailing P/E of 35.4x sits far above the 10-18x sector band, with the stock at 86% of its 52-week range, so it is expensive despite a strong 27% ROE and improving leverage (net debt/EBITDA 1.91x). The biggest risk is that the market is paying a premium for headline profit inflated by one-offs, while margins are compressing, next-year earnings estimates are being trimmed (-1.7% over 90 days), and a Rs 2 trillion capex programme must be executed across 13 projects.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Green Energy is India's largest renewable power producer. It runs 20,763 MW of operating capacity, up 24% YoY, with the 30 GW Khavda park at its core, and it sells power under 25-year fixed-tariff contracts. In H1 FY27, revenue rose 27.6% YoY to ₹8,689 cr and PAT rose 17.8% to ₹1,730 cr, a 19.9% margin. H1 minus Q1 implies Q2 revenue of about ₹4,258 cr, faster than Q1's +16.6%, but Q2 PAT margin of about 17.5% is below Q1's 22.2%. The 'expanding margin' signal compares half-year, full-year and nine-month figures, so it is not like-for-like and overstates the improvement. This is a capital-intensive business, so I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, and on that basis it is expensive. EV/EBITDA is 31.8x against a utilities peer median of 11.6x, the highest in the group. Price-to-book is 12.7x while ROE is only 7.6%, and the stock sits at 93.6% of its 52-week range. Sell-side earnings estimates have been cut 14.5% over 90 days even though 9 of 10 analysts still rate it a buy, a pattern that often comes before a re-rating lower. The main risk is the balance sheet: net debt is 5.6x run-rate EBITDA, gross debt is ₹1.12 lakh cr and H1 free cash flow was -₹7,141 cr, so the equity depends on capacity coming online on time and on cheap refinancing. That is happening while US yields are at 5% and the rupee is weakening.

Lodha (Macrotech) is one of India's largest residential developers, mainly in Mumbai (MMR) and Pune, and is expanding into Bangalore and rental income (annuity assets and data centres). Its reported numbers look strong: H1 FY27 revenue was ₹9,464 cr (+29.8% YoY) and PAT was ₹2,387 cr (+62.9%), with PAT margin up to about 25% from 20% in FY26. But revenue growth slowed from +43% in Q1 to roughly +30% for the half, and in this sector reported profit reflects sales booked 2–4 years ago. The forward-looking numbers are weaker: pre-sales were ₹96.7bn, up only 7% YoY, and collections fell 7%. Hitting the ₹240bn FY27 pre-sales guidance means H2 must deliver about ₹143bn, roughly 1.5x H1, which depends heavily on launching a ₹190.7bn H2 pipeline on time. On valuation I used the sector yardstick, EV/pre-sales, rather than P/E: an enterprise value of about ₹95k cr is roughly 4x guided FY27 pre-sales, or about 4.9x H1 annualised. P/B of 3.9x with ROE of 15.7% and a trailing P/E of 26.5x (inside the 20–35x real estate range and P34 vs the broad market) support a 'fair' grade. The stock sits at 29% of its 52-week range and earnings estimates are being raised, so the entry point is reasonable but not a bargain. The biggest risk is that slow pre-sales and falling collections signal the plateau typical of a late upcycle, and a shortfall against the back-ended guidance would hit the stock.

fundamental.thesis: Canara Bank is a large public sector bank (62.93% GoI ownership) and one of India's top-5 lenders by advances (₹13.6L cr), with a franchise spanning retail, wholesale, and treasury segments; the key yardstick here is P/B vs ROE, per the sector card, not P/E. H1FY27 shows a notable bifurcation: PAT grew strongly +31.3% YoY to ₹10,562 cr on dramatically improved asset quality (Gross NPA 1.33%, Net NPA 0.30%, PCR 95.34%), but total income contracted -3.38% YoY — revenue trajectory has decelerated from +7.7% (FY26) to -3.4% (H1FY27), driven by treasury revenue declining -18% YoY and NIM compression (2.06% FY26 vs 2.51% in Q4FY26), while PAT margin has expanded from 11.7% (FY26) to 13.1% (H1FY27) on sharply lower credit costs. At P/B of 1.02× against ROE of 15.9%, the stock is unambiguously cheap by the sector card's prescribed lender yardstick — sector card benchmark is P/B < 1.5 with ROE > 12% = cheap — and sits at P0 (cheapest) in its 14-peer regional bank cohort on both trailing P/E (6.1×, -64% vs median 16.8×) and forward P/E (5.7×), though much of this structural discount is explained by PSU overhang and below-median CASA (29.86% vs private sector ~40%+). The single biggest risk is NIM pressure persisting through the deposit repricing cycle — NIM at 2.06% for FY26 is already thin for a PSU bank and any further compression from EBLR-linked loan repricing faster than deposit cost decline would erode the PAT margin expansion thesis and keep revenue growth negative.

Britannia is one of India's leading packaged-foods companies, a market leader in biscuits with a growing presence in dairy, cakes and rusk. Q2 FY27, worked out as H1 FY27 minus Q1, had revenue of about ₹5,598 cr, up roughly 15.6% YoY (the press release says consolidated sales grew 16.6%). That is faster than the +7–8% of the prior three quarters. But PAT growth has slowed from +21.1% in Q4 FY26 to +14.1% in Q1 and about +10.8% in Q2 (≈₹726 cr), and gross margin fell from about 46% in FY26 to 41.5% in Q1. Revenue is speeding up while profits are not keeping pace, which suggests input costs or price cuts are eating into margins. The filings do not give volume growth, so we cannot confirm how much of the sales jump is real demand. On the FMCG yardstick of P/E against the 40–65× sector norm, the trailing P/E of 48.4× (forward 39.1×) sits inside the band and at only the P42 percentile among 12 peers, with EV/EBITDA of 34.6× in line with the peer median. That makes it fairly valued, and the stock is near its 52-week low (4.8% of its range). The balance sheet has weakened in H1: inventory rose by about ₹975 cr, short-term borrowings more than doubled to ₹2,440 cr, net debt is about ₹2,175 cr (≈1.1× EBITDA), and only 0.71× of PAT came through as operating cash.

fundamental.thesis: Marico is a leading Indian FMCG company built on Parachute coconut oil, Saffola and value-added hair oils, with growing Foods and digital-first brands and about a quarter of revenue from international markets (Bangladesh, Vietnam, MENA). Q1 FY27 was strong: India volumes grew 11%, India revenue grew about 21%, Parachute gained 400 bps of volume share, and EBITDA margin rose 40 bps to 20.7%. The extracted Q2 FY27 numbers do not hold together, though. Revenue of ₹2,722 cr (+8.4% YoY) sits below Q1's ₹3,957 cr, and PAT of ₹683 cr (+71.6%) is a 25.1% margin that includes ₹133 cr of minority interest and unitemised exceptional items, so the apparent slowdown in growth and jump in margin cannot be trusted until the full results PDF is checked. I graded valuation on P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers: trailing P/E is 59.4x, at the top of the 40–65x FMCG norm, but it is the most expensive in its peer group (P100) at +35.5% above the 43.8x median, EV/EBITDA is 44.1x (+42% vs peers), and the stock is at 80% of its 52-week range, so valuation is expensive even though forward P/E of 42.9x implies earnings growth. The biggest risk is a de-rating: if Q2 shows real slowing in volume or value growth, a stock priced at a premium to every peer has little room for error, and rising crude (an input-cost risk for packaging and some raw materials) adds pressure on margins.

fundamental.thesis: Berger Paints is India's number-two decorative paints maker, with growing industrial, construction-chemical and international businesses, and it says its market share stayed stable through Q2 even as Birla Opus pushes into the market. Revenue growth has sped up from +0.4% YoY in Q3FY26 to +6.7% in Q4FY26, +12.0% in Q1FY27 and +13.2% in Q2FY27. H1FY27 revenue was ₹6,784 cr (+12.5%) and PAT ₹622 cr (+19.3%). Margins are moving the other way: subtracting Q1 from H1 gives Q2 revenue of about ₹3,200 cr and PAT of about ₹217 cr, a PAT margin near 6.8% against 11.3% in Q1. Q2 operating profit grew only 5.2% and standalone EBITDA margin fell 4.4pp because of sharp raw-material inflation and higher ad spend. Because paints are a consumer franchise, I graded valuation on P/E against the sector card's 30–60× band rather than against steel and metals stocks: a trailing P/E of 50.9× (38.7× forward) is fair, though top quartile within Materials (P87), and it sits below the priciest peers ASIANPAINT and PIDILITIND. The 52-week position is mid-range at 48%. The biggest risk is that management sees no easing in input costs and is relying on further price increases from November, while a new entrant makes it harder to pass costs on. Cash conversion is also very weak, with H1 CFO/PAT at 0.23x and free cash flow of -₹82 cr.

fundamental.thesis: Lupin is a large Indian generics maker. It ranks 3rd in the US by prescriptions with about 5% share of generic prescriptions, and its India business is 66% chronic therapies, where it is growing faster than the market (anti-diabetes +28.6% vs +18.8%, chronic +19.5% vs +17.2%). Growth is slowing and profit is shrinking: Q2 FY27 revenue was about ₹7,827 cr (an estimated +11% YoY, down from +32.1% in Q1 and partly helped by the VISUfarma acquisition), Q2 PAT fell 24.6% YoY to about ₹1,186 cr, and H1 PAT fell 10.9% even though revenue grew 20.9%. Margins are contracting: EBITDA margin went from 31.5% in FY26 to 29.5% in H1, pharma operating margin from 26.5% to 22.9%, and the tax rate rose to 26.7%. On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for a manufacturing generics business, Lupin looks cheap: 12.4x, 42% below the peer median of 21.4x (P8), with a trailing P/E of 19.4x against a sector range of 28–40x. Cash conversion is strong (CFO/PAT 1.12x) and net debt/EBITDA is low at 0.44x. The discount looks partly deserved, though: forward P/E (22.1x) is above trailing P/E, analysts have cut FY EPS estimates 5.5% over 90 days, and the US exposure keeps it in the sector's tariff-review headline risk.

Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per the sector card), FACT trades at 120.63× vs a fertilizer/chemicals cyclical mid-cycle norm of 5–8×, ranks P99 among 403 broad-market peers, and carries a P/B of 36.81× on a near-zero ROE — this is unambiguously expensive; the ₹50,886 cr market cap is disconnected from any demonstrated earnings power. The single largest risk is the compounding of a post-Q1 raw-material supply shock (West Asia geopolitical disruptions already causing plant shutdowns) on top of extreme financial leverage (D/E 295×) where quarterly finance costs of ₹61.98 cr structurally exceed operating income, leaving zero buffer for further stress.

Using EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for chemical cyclicals, the stock is expensive at 32.6x against a 5-8x mid-cycle norm, and 83.7x trailing P/E, 42.1x forward P/E and 4.4x P/B on just 5.8% ROE support that view, though the peer ranks (P89 on trailing P/E) use a broad-market fallback rather than close peers, and the 12% dividend yield and 40.34 debt/equity look unreliable, so I did not rely on them. Q2 FY27 figures, derived by subtracting Q1 from H1, show revenue of about Rs 2,631 cr (+43.2% YoY, up from +35.2% in Q1) and PAT of about Rs 462 cr (+31.0%, down from +53.3%), while EBITDA margin fell from 35.1% to about 28.8% YoY; growth was about +20% in FY26 before the deal, and organic growth is not disclosed in the data provided, so the acceleration may be largely acquired, and the 'expanding' PAT margin signal is unreliable because it rests on a likely erroneous Q1 FY26 revenue figure of Rs 182 cr, with PAT margin actually slipping from 19.1% in Q1 to about 17.6% in Q2. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for a capital-intensive business, 20.5x is about 12% below the broad-market median (P44), and trailing P/E of 31.4x sits inside the 28-45x sector range, so valuation is fair, though the peer set is not a close comparison, order-book data needed for the sector card's framework is missing, and the 14.0% dividend yield and the +26% upside to the consensus target look unreliable (market cap and 52-week position suggest a price nearer Rs 1,057, or only about 5% upside). The biggest risk is funding: H1 free cash flow was Rs -733 cr, with operating cash flow of Rs 669 cr against capex of Rs 1,402 cr, before the newly approved Rs 5,947 cr ingot and wafer project, while margins are falling and Rs 2,422 cr of Transcon goodwill is on the balance sheet.

fundamental.thesis: Nuvoco Vistas is an East- and North-focused cement and ready-mix concrete (RMC) maker with about 35 MTPA of target capacity. It is a mid-tier player in a sector where UltraTech and Adani now control about 45% of capacity. Profit quality is thinner than the headline suggests. PAT rose 78% YoY, but only to ₹65 cr, a 2.3% margin. EBITDA margin fell to 14.7% from 18.3% in Q1 and 15.1% a year ago. Implied EBITDA per tonne is about ₹875, below the healthy ₹900–1,100 band and down from roughly ₹1,080 in Q1. Valuation is graded on EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive cement maker, not P/E. At 8.6x (P8 of the broad market, no close peers in the universe), with P/B of 1.09x, forward P/E of 20.5x against trailing 31x, and the price at 18% of its 52-week range, the stock looks cheap against typical cement multiples. Much of that discount is justified by an ROE of only 3.7% and high debt. The biggest risk is the balance sheet. Net debt is ₹5,028 cr, current ratio is 0.57x, free cash flow was -₹246 cr in H1 because of capex, and legal disputes are pending: the ₹490 cr CCI penalty and about ₹454 cr of West Bengal incentive provisions. These come on top of rising crude and a weak rupee pushing up fuel and freight costs.

At trailing P/E of 54.93×, Bikaji sits within the FMCG sector benchmark of 40–65× and is graded FAIR; the forward P/E of 39.26× implies ~40% earnings recovery is already priced in, but the stock is at 0.4% of its 52-week range (near lows) and sell-side EPS estimates have been cut -5.5% over 90 days despite unanimous buy ratings — a pre-derating warning the data feed does not yet reflect in targets. The biggest risk is that sustained margin compression combined with falling estimates converts into earnings misses in Q2FY27 onward, triggering multiple derating from elevated multiples alongside an elevated debt/equity load (17.53× as flagged, though seemingly inconsistent with modest finance costs of ₹5 cr/quarter and warrants verification against filings).

fundamental.thesis: Tata Elxsi is a Tata Group engineering R&D services company specialising in embedded systems design for automotive, media & entertainment, and healthcare verticals — a niche deep-tech services player distinct from commodity IT outsourcers, with a strong domestic and global client base in high-complexity design programmes. Revenue growth has inflected sharply from a -3.9% trough in Q2FY26 to +14.7% YoY in H1FY27 (₹2,077 cr), with PAT rising +13.9% to ₹341 cr and PAT margin holding steady at 16.4%; the System Integration segment contributed 28.9% YoY growth, signalling service diversification — however, EBITDA margin has contracted ~290 bps from its peak of 28.1% (Q3FY26) to 25.2% (H1FY27), driven by New Labour Code wage provisions and rising employee benefits costs. Trailing P/E of 40.78× is above the IT sector benchmark upper bound of 30× (expensive on that metric alone), but the forward P/E collapses to 26.22× — within the 22–30× sector range, confirming earnings recovery is priced in — and peer-rank analysis places TATAELXSI at P60 on both trailing and forward P/E (fairly valued per the ≥P75 expensive threshold); at 6.7% of its 52-week range the stock appears sentiment-oversold relative to an improving earnings trajectory, consistent with the FY26 exceptional charge now cycling out of the base. The primary risk is sustained EBITDA margin compression from structural wage inflation and New Labour Code costs, amplified by a persistent negative EPS revision trend (-0.9% over 90 days, -1.2% next-FY) that historically flags further analyst downgrades ahead, and a long-run AI-driven structural threat to engineering services demand that the sector card explicitly flags as unproven in revenue terms.

Two further cautions: the pre-computed 'accelerating' label compares one quarter to a full year, and the yfinance quarterly revenue (₹1,274 cr) does not reconcile with the filings, so this is not a clean multi-quarter acceleration. On valuation (yardstick: trailing P/E plus EV/EBITDA for IT services), a trailing P/E of 56.0x is well above the 22–30x IT range, EV/EBITDA of 39.6x sits at P82 vs peers, and the stock is at 89% of its 52-week range. fundamental.thesis: UCO Bank is a mid-sized, government-owned lender with gross advances of ₹2,87,690 cr. Its loan book is growing faster each quarter (+16.6% YoY in Q2FY26, +21.2% in Q1FY27, +24.7% in Q2FY27). Q2FY27 net profit rose 26.8% YoY to ₹786 cr, up from +8.1% growth in Q1FY27, and asset quality kept improving: gross NPA fell from 2.56% to 1.96% and net NPA from 0.43% to 0.18% over four quarters, with provision coverage at 98.4%. Net interest income (NII) of ₹2,886 cr is about 13.9% above the year-ago revenue line of ₹2,533 cr, but that row may not be strictly NII, so treat the growth figure as approximate. For a bank we judge value on price-to-book (P/B) against return on equity (ROE), not P/E. P/B of 1.05x is cheap against the market and peers, but ROE is only 8.6% and return on assets 0.8%, well below the 12% ROE needed to call it cheap, so we grade it fair; the 12.7x trailing P/E against a 20.0x forward P/E also suggests the market expects earnings to fall. The biggest risk is funding: loans are growing about 25% while CASA (current and savings account) deposits grow only 10.6%. As a result, the CASA ratio slid from 38.65% to 36.77% and the credit-to-deposit ratio jumped from 75.5% to 82.3%. That pressures margins as the bank pays more for deposits, and it comes in a risk-off market where foreign investors are selling financials.

fundamental.thesis: Tata Motors (TMCV) is India's largest commercial vehicle maker, with 36.2% domestic share in H1 FY27 and 55.7% in heavy trucks, and it holds net cash of Rs 15,900 cr before the Iveco deal. Revenue growth accelerated from +16.1% in Q3 FY26 to +19.3% in Q1 FY27 and +36.3% in Q2 FY27 (Rs 25,338 cr on 42% wholesale volume growth), but EBITDA margin slipped from 11.3% to 10.9% YoY and PAT fell from Rs 2,556 cr in Q1 to Rs 1,253 cr in Q2 (5.0% margin) after a Rs 708 cr fair-value loss; management guides to tapering growth and a 150-200 bps commodity headwind in Q3, so the pre-computed 'expanding' PAT margin signal and the 17.1% Q1 EBITDA margin (it conflicts with 10.9% for both H1 and Q2) should not be relied on. Valuation is fair using EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for this capital-intensive business: 16.8x is 28% below the broad-market median of 23.3x (P30), and forward P/E of 18.5x sits at the low end of the 18-28x auto range with estimates up 10.1% over 90 days, but the trailing P/E of 49.5x (distorted by fair-value losses) and P/B of 11.8x (P87) limit the cheapness case, and the peer set is a broad-market fallback rather than true CV peers. The biggest risk is the Iveco acquisition, whose final tender outcome, funding and integration burden are not visible in the data provided and could erode the net cash position just as the CV cycle's growth rates are guided to slow, while the auditor resignation filed on 2026-10-31 remains unexplained here.

fundamental.thesis: Hindustan Copper (HINDCOPPER) is India's only vertically integrated copper mining and smelting PSU, with a near-monopoly on domestic copper ore mining and implicit government backing as a strategic-metal producer. Q1FY27 delivered revenue of ₹936cr (+81.4% YoY) and PAT of ₹352cr (+162.5% YoY), with PAT margin expanding sharply to 37.6% from 26.0% a year ago and EBITDA margin surging to 56%; growth has clearly accelerated from a muted +4.6% YoY in Q1FY26, driven overwhelmingly by higher copper realisations rather than volume — a commodity-price-lift story, not a structural earnings re-rating. Using EV/EBITDA as the correct yardstick for a capital-intensive commodity cyclical (per sector card), HINDCOPPER trades at 33.4× — more than 4× the mid-cycle cyclical benchmark of 5–8× and +43% above the broad-market median (P70); trailing P/E of 53.5× is also far above the Materials sector range of 12–22×, grading the stock as expensive. fundamental.thesis: Eicher Motors is India's dominant mid-weight motorcycle manufacturer through Royal Enfield (87% domestic market share in the segment) with an expanding global footprint and a 50:50 JV in VECV (commercial vehicles), giving it a structurally premium and defensible franchise. Q1FY27 revenue surged 31.6% YoY to ₹6,632 cr with PAT up 21.4% to ₹1,463 cr — however, PAT margin compressed 181 bps YoY to 22.0%, and the PAT growth meaningfully lagging revenue growth signals cost absorption headwinds despite strong volumes; the EBITDA margin trend is more encouraging, expanding to 31.0% in Q1FY27 from ~24–25% in mid-FY26, suggesting operating leverage is materialising at the gross level even as below-the-line costs (finance, depreciation from capex ramp) create PAT drag. On the sector-preferred P/E yardstick, trailing P/E of 37.9× sits at the P80 peer percentile and commands a 40% premium to the sector median of 27.1×; EV/EBITDA at 33.7× is P100 in its peer set and 84% above the sector median — on both measures the stock is expensive relative to peers, and the forward P/E of 28.8× (still P83) reflects already-priced-in earnings growth, leaving limited re-rating room. The key risk is the combination of a RISK_OFF macro (FII selling, rising crude costs for consumers, Auto sector underweight tilt) with a stock already in the top quartile of peer valuations and PAT margins visibly compressing — any festive season demand disappointment or further input cost spike would catalyse a derating without a valuation cushion.

Using the FMCG card's P/E norm of 40-65x as the main yardstick, 59.4x trailing P/E is within the band but near its top, and I grade it expensive because earnings are falling, it ranks P78 on P/E against a broad-market peer set with no close comparables, EV/EBITDA is 33.3x, and the 40.5x forward P/E relies on estimates already cut 16.1% for the current year in 30 days; being only 13.3% above the 52-week low does not by itself make it good value. The biggest risk is that the margin drop proves structural rather than temporary, as the filings data here does not explain the cause, while H1 free cash flow was Rs -106 cr with capex at 15.7% of revenue and the Company Secretary resigned on results day.

fundamental.thesis: Deepak Fertilisers is a mid-cap ammonia-chain business. It makes industrial chemicals (nitric acid, IPA, methanol), it is a leading Indian producer of technical ammonium nitrate (TAN) for mining, and it sells crop nutrition (NPK, specialty fertilisers), with large new capacity at Gopalpur (TAN) and Dahej (nitric acid) due to start in Q2 FY27. On the official filings, FY26 revenue grew 12.0% to ₹11,506 cr, but PAT fell 21.8% to ₹739 cr. Profitability has been shrinking through the year: PAT margin slid from 8.1% (H1) to 7.0% (9M) to 6.4% (full year), and EBITDA margin from 17.3% to 14.6%. The filing-extracted trend table has no Q1 FY27 revenue or PAT, and the unverified yfinance figure (PAT ₹490 cr on ₹1,886 cr revenue) looks like it may include a one-off. Treating this as a cyclical chemicals business, we judge it on EV/EBITDA: 11.1× is about half the broad-market median (bottom 15% of the market), but it is above the 5–8× the sector card calls normal for chemical cyclicals at mid-cycle. Trailing P/E of 16.9× sits inside the 12–22× Materials range, so overall we grade it fair. The forward P/E of 10.6× and analysts raising this year's earnings estimates by 43% over 30 days already assume the new plants succeed. The biggest risks are a slow ramp-up at the new plants with debt high (debt/equity about 0.76) and free cash flow negative (−₹396 cr in H1 FY26), together with raw-material squeeze from the Middle East and a falling-margin trend.

fundamental.thesis: India Cements is a mid-sized South India cement maker with 14.75 MT of capacity (Q1FY26). It is now controlled by UltraTech, so the story depends on a turnaround under new ownership rather than on stand-alone strength. The latest extracted figures are stale: they run only to 9MFY26 (filed Jan-2026), and the Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-10-17 have not been indexed yet. In those older numbers, cumulative revenue growth picked up from -0.2% YoY in Q1FY26 to +4.8% in H1FY26 and +10.9% in 9MFY26 (₹3,256 cr). The company was still losing money, though the loss margin narrowed from -13.0% to -3.9% (9M PAT ₹-127 cr), while EBITDA margin slipped from 9.4% (H1) to 7.5% (9M), so the fall in costs per rupee of sales has not held. Because cement is capital-intensive, I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA. At 25.9× it sits well above normal cement multiples and above the broad-market median of 23.3×, and the 116× trailing P/E reflects barely positive earnings. The 1.06× P/B and the price near its 52-week low look cheap only on the surface. The 20.6× forward P/E already assumes a turnaround, while analysts have cut this year's EPS estimates by about 21% in the last 30 days. Grade: expensive. The biggest risk is that EBITDA per tonne keeps lagging the healthy ₹900–1,100 band. Rising crude-linked fuel and freight costs and a risk-off market make that more likely, and the turnaround that today's price assumes would then be pushed back.

fundamental.thesis: SAIL is a large government-owned integrated steel maker, with Bhilai, Bokaro and Rourkela contributing about 81% of revenue, and it benefits from India's protected steel upcycle. H1 FY27 revenue rose 10.7% YoY to Rs 58,243 cr, improving from about +8% in H1 FY26, while EBITDA margin edged up from 10.9% to 11.5%; PAT jumped about 192% to Rs 3,395 cr, but EBITDA rose only about 14% (roughly Rs 840 cr against a PAT gain above Rs 2,200 cr), so the jump is not explained by operations, and the missing Q1 FY27 row means Q2 momentum cannot be isolated. On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital-intensive steel, the 8.84x snapshot is slightly above the 5-8x mid-cycle norm, while the 22.3x trailing P/E looks stale because filing-based trailing PAT of about Rs 5,516 cr implies about 13.6x, so I grade it fair: P/B of 1.3x with about 10.9% annualised ROE is not a clear bargain, the broad-market peer ranks are a weak comparison, and rising estimates (FY EPS +18.5% over 30 days) are offset by little upside, since the Rs 185 mean target is only about 2% above the roughly Rs 182 price implied by the 52-week position, not the stated 13.2%. The biggest risk is that the PAT surge proves non-recurring or steel spreads narrow, and no spread or EBITDA-per-tonne data was available to test this, with Rs 23,457 cr of provisionally priced government sales and a 0.79 current ratio adding balance-sheet risk.

Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation is a Gujarat-based mining company, mainly lignite, with a smaller power segment that remains low-margin (6.4% in Q2 FY27). Q2 FY27 revenue rose 71.2% YoY to Rs 903 cr, accelerating from +23.8% in Q1 and about -11% in 9M FY26 off a low base, but it was flat QoQ (Rs 907 cr); reported PAT fell 63.3% to Rs 171 cr only because Q2 FY26 included a Rs 474 cr GST credit, with underlying PAT up about 27% and PAT margin of 18.9% below the roughly 23% of Q3 FY26. Using EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive commodity business, the stock looks expensive at the feed's 43.9x (P85 vs the broad market), and even my rough market-cap-to-FY26-EBITDA estimate of about 23x is far above the sector card's 5-8x mid-cycle range for cyclicals; the 20.6x trailing P/E and CHEAP peer verdict are flattered by the FY26 one-off, as PAT for the last four quarters of about Rs 663 cr implies roughly 30x. The biggest risk is that profit keeps lagging revenue while the valuation already assumes strong growth, and conviction is held back by missing Q2 EBITDA, no management guidance, and implausible feed data (163% dividend yield, 4.47 debt/equity that may be a percentage, and a yfinance Q2 revenue of Rs 538 cr that conflicts with the filing's Rs 903 cr).

fundamental.thesis: Crompton is one of India's largest fan, pump and small-appliance makers. fundamental.thesis: UPL is India's largest global agrochemical company, operating crop protection (UPL Corp), seeds (Advanta), and post-harvest segments across 130+ countries — a capital-intensive, leveraged cyclical recovering from a multi-year agrochem destocking cycle. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card guidance), UPL at 7.86× sits at P6 vs. 473 broad-market peers (67% discount to the 23.3× median) and at the mid-cycle floor for specialty chemicals (5–8× range); forward P/E of 12.65× is 46% below trailing 27.34×, signalling substantial earnings recovery priced in — the stock grades cheap on the appropriate metric. fundamental.thesis: Sagility is a mid-cap healthcare outsourcing company. About 90% of revenue comes from US health insurers (payers) and about 10% from hospitals and other providers. fundamental.thesis: E.I.D. Parry is mainly a farm-inputs group: nutrients and crop protection through its subsidiary CIL made up about 90% of Q1 FY27 segment revenue, with sugar, distillery, nutraceuticals and consumer products much smaller, so the FMCG tag and P/E norms fit poorly. Revenue growth has slowed from +29.3% in Q1 FY26 to +18.3% in Q3 FY26 and +3.4% (Rs 9,018 cr) in Q1 FY27, with the NACL acquisition's boost lapsing from August 2026, while PAT fell 42.5% to Rs 142 cr, EBITDA margin slipped from 10.3% to 8.7%, sugar revenue fell 62% after the refinery closure, and distillery revenue fell 13.5%. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick, with P/B as a cross-check, the stock looks cheap at 5.96x (P2 of the broad market, with no tight peers) and 1.53x book, despite a less clear 29.06x trailing P/E, but consolidated multiples include profit owed to minority holders, some discount looks earned, and the 10.1x forward P/E rests on one analyst whose estimates were cut about 30% in 90 days. The biggest risk is that low price masks weak earnings quality, as FY26 CFO/PAT was only 0.02x, FCF was Rs -64 cr, and the Q2 FY27 results due on 13 Nov could bring further cuts; some extracted figures also look unreliable, including the Rs 61,000 cr refinery investment, the 23.65 debt/equity reading (possibly 23.65%, or about 0.24x) and the +67.6% target upside (about +39% at the implied price near Rs 756).

fundamental.thesis: ZF CVCS India is a domestic-content auto ancillary supplying braking, transmission (AMT), and safety control systems for commercial vehicles, with a structural EV angle as the sole OEM e-compressor supplier for electric buses — a meaningful ASP story given e-bus kits cost ~₹2.25L vs ~₹45K for standard CV kits (~5× uplift). Q1FY27 revenue grew +9.3% YoY to ₹1,066 cr (a recovery from flat FY25 and near-zero H1 FY26), but PAT fell 14.6% YoY to ₹104 cr (9.8% margin) as EBITDA margin compressed 505 bps from 20.3% to 16.3% — textbook negative operating leverage; the margin trajectory has been consistently contracting from 22.9% (Q2FY26) through 20.0% (Q3FY26) to 16.3% (Q1FY27) and is the dominant concern. The valuation snapshot's trailing P/E of 2.83× is almost certainly corrupted by the June 2026 5:1 bonus split distorting yfinance EPS; using trend-table LTM PAT of ~₹498 cr against ₹29,000 cr market cap implies an estimated trailing P/E of ~58×, well above the 18–28× Auto sector median — graded expensive — and the forward P/E of 38.28× (itself above sector median) confirms earnings are expected to remain well below recent peaks. The key risk is that persistent margin compression and 90-day EPS estimate cuts of 5.8%, combined with a CFO transition in September 2026 and a RISK_OFF macro, leave no near-term catalyst for re-rating toward fundamental value.

fundamental.thesis: Netweb Technologies builds high-performance computing systems, AI servers and private-cloud hardware in India, so it is a hardware and infrastructure maker rather than a labour-based IT services firm; the sector card's warning that AI deflates services revenue fits it poorly, and AI capex demand is more likely a tailwind. Q1 FY27 revenue was about ₹714 cr (+174.5% YoY) with PAT of ₹85 cr (+196.5%), and yfinance shows Q2 FY27 at about ₹1,091 cr revenue and ₹137 cr PAT. Rising sell-side estimates (FY EPS +11.8% over 90 days) support momentum but leave little room for any slip in lumpy, order-driven revenue.

fundamental.thesis: ABB India is a leading industrial technology company (electrification + automation) that has restructured by selling its Robotics business (March 2026) and earlier demerging Power Grids to Hitachi Energy, concentrating into two segments with an order book of ₹11,094 cr (book-to-revenue 3.48×, providing ~2 years of visibility). Revenue growth on continuing operations has decelerated from +13.7% to +6.0% over three comparable periods, while continuing-operations EBITDA fell 9.2% YoY (margin compressed from 19.4% to 15.5%) and continuing PAT declined 11.1% to ₹712 cr in H1-26 — the headline PAT of ₹2,146 cr is entirely inflated by a ₹1,658 cr one-time Robotics disposal gain and must be stripped for any true read on the business. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick (per sector card for capital-intensive industrials), ABB trades at 77.8× vs a sector median of 34.0×, ranking at P94 among 17 industrial peers — deeply expensive with no margin of safety even on forward P/E at 67.8× (still +97% premium to sector median). The biggest risk is a 30–50% valuation de-rating (the sector card explicitly flags this as typical on capex-pause fears) accelerated by negative sell-side revisions (FY-EPS -4.4% over 30 days, 13/28 analysts on Sell) and an underlying business showing simultaneous EBITDA compression and Automation segment contraction in a RISK_OFF macro.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol

rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session

books.title: Growth screen (ranked by PAT growth)
books.hypothesis: Avoid what the grades call losers (high risk, weak growth, poor data, decelerating), then buy the highest reported revenue growth — the one fundamental the winners forensic found on the winners' side — with Book 3's construction.

rules.eligible: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)
rules.rank: PAT growth YoY from the filings, highest first (missing last), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass the same filter, else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, or the 120-session review failing (the same filter); no sentiment exit
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)

books.kill_rule: more than 10 points behind the equal-weight null on a rolling 60-date basis, twice in a row
books.promote_rule: best book at 90 dates, if ahead of both benchmarks

brinson.method: Brinson-Fachler vs the equal-weight universe, start-of-month holdings held through the month; Cash is a sector with zero return and zero benchmark weight
